title: Run the Python security patterns
teach: Eight reusable patterns underpin all security automation: parsing tool output, reading nested data, filtering findings, paging an API, CSV reports, retries, CLIs, and a cloud audit.

title: Confirm the Python drills pass
teach: Each pattern has a test. Passing tests are your instant feedback loop while you learn to modify code.

title: Set up and verify the AppSec lab
teach: A deliberately vulnerable Flask app with 10 OWASP flaws, each paired with a fix. First make its tests pass so your environment is ready.
do: cd appsec-lab && python3 -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt && pytest tests/ -q

title: Set up the CTF and read the challenges
teach: The CTF proves your skill: you exploit the target yourself and capture flags. No interaction with anyone needed — the checker grades you.
do: cd ctf-lab && python3 -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt && python ctf.py list

title: Capture your first flag (easy tier)
teach: Start the target in another terminal (python target/run_target.py). Pick an easy challenge (python ctf.py show idor), exploit it, then submit the flag (python ctf.py submit idor 'FLAG{...}').
do: Start target, then: python ctf.py submit idor 'FLAG{...}'

title: Clear the easy tier (4 flags)
teach: Solve idor, sqli, traversal, and xss. Use 'python ctf.py hint <id>' when stuck; walkthroughs/ has full solutions as a last resort.

title: Capture all 8 flags
teach: Finish the medium and hard tiers: forgeable session, SSRF to metadata, command injection, and JWT alg:none. This is a genuine, self-graded skills checkpoint.

title: Run the cloud exposure auditor
teach: Turn cloud knowledge into automated checks: public buckets, open security groups, IAM wildcards, unencrypted/public databases, missing CloudTrail.
do: cd cloud-security-lab && python3 -m auditor.audit data/sample_account.json --fail-on HIGH

title: Scan a Terraform plan
teach: Catch misconfiguration before deploy. The scanner reads a terraform plan and flags public storage, open security groups, public/unencrypted databases, and IAM admin wildcards.

title: Validate container and Kubernetes hardening
teach: The validators flag privileged pods, running as root, writable root filesystems, missing limits, and risky Dockerfiles. The tests show insecure vs hardened.

title: Analyze an SBOM for risky dependencies
teach: A software bill of materials lets you answer 'are we affected by this CVE?'. The analyzer flags vulnerable and unpinned components.

title: Run the release gate
teach: The capstone: aggregate findings from Semgrep, Trivy, and Gitleaks, apply a policy, and block the release. This is the DevSecOps decision most engineers miss.
do: cd devsecops-lab && python3 -m gate.run_gate --semgrep samples/semgrep_sample.json --trivy samples/trivy_sample.json --gitleaks samples/gitleaks_sample.json --fail-on HIGH

verify.cmd: python3 -m gate.run_gate --semgrep samples/semgrep_sample.json --trivy samples/trivy_sample.json --gitleaks samples/gitleaks_sample.json --fail-on HIGH

title: Attack and defend an AI assistant
teach: The OWASP Top 10 for LLM apps: prompt injection, insecure output handling, secret disclosure, and excessive agency. The demo shows each attack succeed, then be blocked by guardrails.

title: Verify the LLM guardrails
teach: Each guardrail (injection screening, output encoding, secret redaction, tool authorization) has a test proving the attack is blocked.

title: Detect attacks in security logs
teach: The blue-team side: detection rules over logs catch brute force, SQLi, path traversal, privilege escalation, and impossible travel. This is core SOC / detection-engineering work.

title: Verify the detection rules
teach: Each rule is tested two ways: it must fire on the attack and stay quiet on benign traffic. That paired test is what makes a detection production-ready.
